snapshots.source_name: Roy Morgan Federal Voting Intention
snapshots.captured_representation: Roy Morgan federal voting intention published 7 September 2026; fieldwork 31 August to 6 September 2026; sample size 1,541; primary vote: Labor 27.0%, One Nation 26.5%, Liberal 17.0%, Greens 14.5%, Nationals 4.5%.
snapshots.notes: Primary polling snapshot already used by the public form ladder; now entered into the forward source register.

snapshots.source_name: Australian Greens — federal team and portfolio announcement
snapshots.captured_representation: Australian Greens announced on 7 September 2026 that Vanessa Bleyer joined the federal team after Pete Whish-Wilson's departure; Bleyer took Agriculture, Science/Industry/Innovation, Tourism and Healthy Oceans portfolios; David Shoebridge became spokesperson for Digital Rights and AI.
snapshots.notes: Primary party source; records party and actor role changes.

snapshots.source_name: Liberal Party of Australia — Coalition illicit tobacco policy
snapshots.captured_representation: The Liberal Party published a Coalition policy on 3 September 2026 proposing an 80% cut to tobacco excise, legalisation/regulation/taxation of vapes and nicotine pouches for adults, and a $200 million nationwide law-enforcement surge against illicit tobacco.
snapshots.notes: Primary party source. Joint Coalition policy is attached to Liberal and Nationals state events without collapsing the parties into one team.

snapshots.source_name: Pauline Hanson's One Nation — tobacco policy
snapshots.captured_representation: One Nation published a tobacco policy on 1 September 2026 proposing a 75% cut to tobacco excise, a three-year pause in indexation, and tougher action against organised crime and illicit tobacco.
snapshots.notes: Primary party source. Underlying numerical claims in the release are not independently promoted to verified facts by this snapshot.

snapshots.source_name: Australian Labor Party — housing supply release
snapshots.captured_representation: Australian Labor Party published on 21 August 2026 that the 100th residential housing development had received approval under the EPBC Act and stated that more than 80,000 new homes had been given the green light under national environmental law under the government to date.
snapshots.notes: Primary party/government-position source. The snapshot verifies the published position; numerical claims remain attributed to the release unless separately corroborated.

snapshots.source_name: Australian Greens Federal MPs media release index
snapshots.captured_representation: Australian Greens federal media releases page on 8 September 2026 showed multiple releases dated 7 September 2026, including the Vanessa Bleyer federal-team announcement and David Shoebridge's formal announcement as spokesperson on Digital Rights and AI.
snapshots.notes: Index-level capture used to corroborate publication timing and current portfolio announcement activity.

snapshots.source_name: Liberal Party of Australia — tobacco-tax release
snapshots.captured_representation: The Liberal Party of Australia published on 8 September 2026 a release titled 'Minns defies Albanese on tobacco tax as PM refuses to act', attributing to NSW Premier Chris Minns the view that current tobacco tax settings were not working and framing the comments as a policy split within Labor.
snapshots.notes: Primary party source. This snapshot verifies the Liberal Party publication and its framing; it does not independently promote every underlying claim in the release to fact.

snapshots.source_name: NSW Government — Woollahra housing transformation release
snapshots.captured_representation: NSW Government published on 8 September 2026 a ministerial release titled 'First look: Woollahra long-term housing transformation', announcing public exhibition of a draft rezoning proposal around Woollahra and Edgecliff that it says could support up to 9,400 new homes.
snapshots.notes: Primary government source. The release and public-exhibition state are observed; projections and claimed dwelling capacity remain attributed to the source.

snapshots.notes: Primary party forward campaign-activity source. Candidate identities and event details are recorded as attributed party publication facts.

Latest News and Updates - Pauline Hanson One Nation Follow us for the latest news and updates from Pauline Hanson's One Nation. If you want to stay ahead with stories about important issues, politics, election events, and breaking news you can find it here. http://www.onenation.org.au/news Follow One Nation NSW Leader Mike Newman on Facebook

Mike Newman, our new leader in NSW, now has his own Facebook page.

Tue, 08 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/mike-newman-facebook Albanese Calls Super a ‘National Asset’ — But It’s Your Money
Anthony Albanese has told a room full of fund managers and bank CEOs that Australia’s $4.5 trillion in retirement savings has “real potential” to be treated as a “national asset.”

Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/super-retirement-savings Pauline Hanson Unveils One Nation’s 3% Super Pay Boost

Senator Pauline Hanson
One Nation Senator for Queensland

MEDIA RELEASE

ONE NATION TO GIVE RENTERS AND MORTGAGE HOLDERS A
3% SUPER PAY BOOST

7 September 2026

One Nation will give Australians paying rent or a mortgage the choice to take one quarter of their future compulsory super contributions as a tax-advantaged 3% pay boost for up to three years.

Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/super-pay-boost One Nation Questions Labor’s New Climate Change ‘Misinformation’ Unit
Climate change propaganda unit!
Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/climate-misinformation-unit Mike Newman Outlines One Nation’s Tough Approach to Crime in NSW

Mike Newman was on 2GB this week outlining his robust, common-sense approach to tackling crime, particularly gang-related crime, in Sydney. We need to give our police the backing they need to do the job.

Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/newman-nsw-crime-plan One Nation Calls for Bondi Icebergs to Be Protected Amid Land Claim Uncertainty
Ongoing uncertainty, it seems, for arguably Australia’s most famous and iconic swimming club.
Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/bondi-icebergs-land-claim One Nation Victoria gets tough on crime

There is no state in Australia where crime has been allowed to get out of control as much as it has in Victoria. Things have got so bad that for a great many Victorians crime is now the number one issue. Bigger than even the cost of living. It is so sad to see what has happened in so many parts of our state, particularly Melbourne. It used to be the crown jewel of Australia. Now, after a decade of woeful leadership by the Labor Party, it is the butt of jokes and derision.

Thu, 03 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/one-nation-victoria-gets-tough-on-crime One nation. One flag. Because we are all Australian.

Written by Colleen Harkin

In recent years, we seem perfectly happy to celebrate every difference – every culture, every group, every identity, every grievance. But suggest that Australia might also be celebrated or that we need a common national identity, and suddenly it becomes controversial. It shouldn't be.

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/one-nation-one-flag One Nation Tobacco Policy Targets Illegal Trade and Organised Crime
The new One Nation policy on tobacco is about cracking down on organised crime and illegal tobacco. It is not about promoting tobacco. Labor’s approach is failing. Between 2017 and 2025, tobacco consumption has risen by approximately 40%. Illicit sources supply about 80% of all nicotine consumed!

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/illegal-tobacco-crime Bush Summit: One Nation Says Food Security Is National Security
Food security is national security.

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/bush-summit One Nation Celebrates Landslide Victory in Secret Harbour
Landslide victory in Secret Harbour!

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/secret-harbour-landslide Mike Newman Steps Up as One Nation’s NSW Leader
Our new One Nation NSW leader for the state election in March is the real deal.

Mon, 31 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/mike-newman-nsw-leader One Nation Tasmania Officially Registered as a State Political Party

Written by Lee Hanson

IT’S OFFICIAL — ONE NATION TASMANIA IS REGISTERED!

We are extremely proud to announce that Pauline Hanson’s One Nation is now officially registered as a state political party in Tasmania!

Fri, 28 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/one-nation-tasmania-registered One Nation’s Foreign Terrorist Fighters Bill Wins Strong Support
I guess this won’t come as a massive surprise to most. The vast majority of Aussies back our “Protecting Australians from Foreign Terrorist Fighters Bill.” Another occasion where establishment politicians and the media are completely disconnected from the views of everyday Aussies.
Thu, 27 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/foreign-fighters-bill GetUp! Sets Its Sights on One Nation Victoria
Apparently GetUp! have learnt the lessons from their juvenile stunt at the National Press Club and recent campaign failures. Their new focus is on trying to stop One Nation Victoria.
Wed, 26 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/getup-targets-victoria One Nation: End Political Indoctrination in Australian Schools

Author is: Colleen Harkin, One Nation Victoria candidate, South-East Metro, Legislative Council candidate

Australian parents are being sold a lie about what is happening in our education system.

Instead of concentrating on knowledge, literacy, numeracy, science, history and civics, schools are being used to shape children's beliefs about race, climate, identity, sexuality, inequality and social justice.

Tue, 25 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/education-not-indoctrination Senator Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce Call for Section 18C to Be Scrapped
At the heart of the battle for free speech is section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act. Barnaby was right, it needs to be scrapped. The impact that section 18C has had on free speech in this country and democracy has been chilling. Pauline’s recent court battles have made this very clear. Robust political debate is critical for our democracy.
Tue, 25 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/scrap-section-18c Colleen Harkin: Keep Political Activism Out of Victorian Classrooms

Parliament has passed it. Every school, Prep to Year 12, now has to teach Australian history through the “activism” lens pushed by the Yoorrook Commission.

Mon, 24 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/victoria-history-curriculum Senator Pauline Hanson: Stop Importing Security Risks Into Australia

Pauline has made clear that she doesn’t want us to import the world’s problems at the expense of Australia’s security. That is exactly what is happening right now under this Labor government.

Mon, 24 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/australia-migration-security One Nation Gives Regional Australia a Stronger Voice

Voters across regional Australia are increasingly turning to One Nation. For too long, uniparty politicians have failed our regional communities and our food producers.

Changes to electoral law The Electoral Amendment Act 2026 made some changes to the Electoral Act 2002, the law state elections are run under. The full list of changes is on our Electoral Act amendments page. Some key differences are: the electoral roll closes at 8 pm the day the writ of an election is issued, 1 week earlier than other elections. This year the roll will close at 8 pm on Tuesday 3 November , Melbourne Cup Day. there are fewer days for candidates to nominate. If you're an independent candidate, make sure you're prepared before nominations open on Wednesday 4 November. the early voting period is shorter. This year early voting will be available from Wednesday 18 to Friday 27 November. Changes we have made This year we've made some changes we think will make it easier for all Victorians to actively participate in their democracy. Low sensory voting – there'll be a low-sensory mobile voting session in every district on Tuesday 17 November between 10am and 4pm. We'll share more information about this session later this year. Early voting centres – all early voting centres will also be election day voting centres. This will make it easier to find a voting centre location that works for you. EasyVote guide – we're mailing a printed version of our EasyVote guide to all households. This pamphlet will have all the key information about when, where, and how to vote correctly. Prepare for November Become a candidate Candidate nominations: open at 9 am Wednesday 4 November close at 12 noon on Monday 9 November for all candidates . There is a shorter nomination period this year. If you’re an independent candidate, make sure you’re prepared before nominations open. Independent candidates must nominate in person at the election office of the electorate they’re nominating in. For district (lower house) independent candidates, this will be the district election office. For region (upper house) independent candidates this will be any district election office within your region. From Wednesday 14 October, Candidate Helper will have: nomination forms election office locations opening hours contact information Registered political parties must lodge the nomination forms for their endorsed candidates directly with us. More information Become a state election candidate Know your electorate Victoria is made up of 88 districts and 8 regions. The 88 districts make up Victoria’s lower house of Parliament, the Legislative Assembly. Each district is represented by one Member of Parliament (MP for short). The 8 regions make up Victoria’s upper house of Parliament, the Legislative Council. Each region is represented by 5 Members of Parliament. If you’ve moved house since the 2022 state election, you might be voting in a new electorate. If you do move house, it’s your responsibility to keep your enrolment up to date . Why this is important When candidates nominate for an election, they nominate for either one district or one region. When you go to vote, you’ll be given ballot papers for the district and region you’re enrolled in. If you want to find out more about the candidates who want your vote, you need to know which electorate you’re enrolled in. Knowing your electorate also helps you plan where you go to vote, if you want to vote in person. If you do vote in person, knowing which electorate you’re enrolled in can make it faster for you at the voting centre. More information What are electoral boundaries? Interactive electoral boundaries map Electoral Boundaries Commission Parliament of Victoria website Work at the election Elections are a fundamental part of democracy in Victoria. During a state election, we hire up to 25,000 staff for a range of important jobs. We’re looking for staff from a wide range of backgrounds. In particular want to hear from you if you: speak multiple languages are of Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander background live with a disability are 18-29 years old Many jobs involve working in a voting centre on election day. There are also jobs in the months before and after election day. Apply to work at the election Political donations There are strict laws that regulate political donations in Victoria, including: who can make a political donation the maximum value of political donations when you must disclose political donations you make or receive a ban on foreign donations. There have been recent updates to the political donation laws that all political participants should be aware of. Please read our 2026 political finance laws and political donations pages for the details of these changes. Rules for campaigning You can start campaigning at any time, even before nominations open. When you’re campaigning, you must: properly authorise your electoral material so it’s clear who is accountable for it. The law about authorisations has recently changed so make sure you are familiar with the new rules. follow all non-electoral laws, such as defamation laws not distribute material that’s likely to mislead voters into casting their vote incorrectly follow all political donation disclosure rules as soon as you publicly declare your intention to become a candidate. You must do this even if you don’t end up nominating. If you see something you think is in breach of the Electoral Act 2002 , please submit a complaint . We’ll investigate and, where appropriate, we’ll let you know the outcome. snapshots.captured_representation:
Latest News and Updates - Pauline Hanson One Nation Follow us for the latest news and updates from Pauline Hanson's One Nation. If you want to stay ahead with stories about important issues, politics, election events, and breaking news you can find it here. http://www.onenation.org.au/news Barnaby Joyce Backs Mike Newman to Lead One Nation in NSW

Barnaby describes new One Nation NSW leader Mike Newman as “top shelf”.

Tue, 08 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/barnaby-backs-mike-newman One Nation Questions Why Labor Won’t Show Off Its Net Zero Mega Projects
Labor are ashamed of their net zero scam and there is one dead giveaway.

Tue, 08 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/net-zero-mega-projects Follow One Nation NSW Leader Mike Newman on Facebook

Mike Newman, our new leader in NSW, now has his own Facebook page.

Tue, 08 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/mike-newman-facebook Albanese Calls Super a ‘National Asset’ — But It’s Your Money
Anthony Albanese has told a room full of fund managers and bank CEOs that Australia’s $4.5 trillion in retirement savings has “real potential” to be treated as a “national asset.”

Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/super-retirement-savings Pauline Hanson Unveils One Nation’s 3% Super Pay Boost

Senator Pauline Hanson
One Nation Senator for Queensland

MEDIA RELEASE

ONE NATION TO GIVE RENTERS AND MORTGAGE HOLDERS A
3% SUPER PAY BOOST

7 September 2026

One Nation will give Australians paying rent or a mortgage the choice to take one quarter of their future compulsory super contributions as a tax-advantaged 3% pay boost for up to three years.

Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/super-pay-boost One Nation Questions Labor’s New Climate Change ‘Misinformation’ Unit
Climate change propaganda unit!
Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/climate-misinformation-unit Mike Newman Outlines One Nation’s Tough Approach to Crime in NSW

Mike Newman was on 2GB this week outlining his robust, common-sense approach to tackling crime, particularly gang-related crime, in Sydney. We need to give our police the backing they need to do the job.

Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/newman-nsw-crime-plan One Nation Calls for Bondi Icebergs to Be Protected Amid Land Claim Uncertainty
Ongoing uncertainty, it seems, for arguably Australia’s most famous and iconic swimming club.
Mon, 07 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/bondi-icebergs-land-claim One Nation Victoria gets tough on crime

There is no state in Australia where crime has been allowed to get out of control as much as it has in Victoria. Things have got so bad that for a great many Victorians crime is now the number one issue. Bigger than even the cost of living. It is so sad to see what has happened in so many parts of our state, particularly Melbourne. It used to be the crown jewel of Australia. Now, after a decade of woeful leadership by the Labor Party, it is the butt of jokes and derision.

Thu, 03 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/one-nation-victoria-gets-tough-on-crime One nation. One flag. Because we are all Australian.

Written by Colleen Harkin

In recent years, we seem perfectly happy to celebrate every difference – every culture, every group, every identity, every grievance. But suggest that Australia might also be celebrated or that we need a common national identity, and suddenly it becomes controversial. It shouldn't be.

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/one-nation-one-flag One Nation Tobacco Policy Targets Illegal Trade and Organised Crime
The new One Nation policy on tobacco is about cracking down on organised crime and illegal tobacco. It is not about promoting tobacco. Labor’s approach is failing. Between 2017 and 2025, tobacco consumption has risen by approximately 40%. Illicit sources supply about 80% of all nicotine consumed!

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/illegal-tobacco-crime Bush Summit: One Nation Says Food Security Is National Security
Food security is national security.

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/bush-summit One Nation Celebrates Landslide Victory in Secret Harbour
Landslide victory in Secret Harbour!

Tue, 01 Sep 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/secret-harbour-landslide Mike Newman Steps Up as One Nation’s NSW Leader
Our new One Nation NSW leader for the state election in March is the real deal.

Mon, 31 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/mike-newman-nsw-leader One Nation Tasmania Officially Registered as a State Political Party

Written by Lee Hanson

IT’S OFFICIAL — ONE NATION TASMANIA IS REGISTERED!

We are extremely proud to announce that Pauline Hanson’s One Nation is now officially registered as a state political party in Tasmania!

Fri, 28 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/one-nation-tasmania-registered One Nation’s Foreign Terrorist Fighters Bill Wins Strong Support
I guess this won’t come as a massive surprise to most. The vast majority of Aussies back our “Protecting Australians from Foreign Terrorist Fighters Bill.” Another occasion where establishment politicians and the media are completely disconnected from the views of everyday Aussies.
Thu, 27 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/foreign-fighters-bill GetUp! Sets Its Sights on One Nation Victoria
Apparently GetUp! have learnt the lessons from their juvenile stunt at the National Press Club and recent campaign failures. Their new focus is on trying to stop One Nation Victoria.
Wed, 26 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/getup-targets-victoria One Nation: End Political Indoctrination in Australian Schools

Author is: Colleen Harkin, One Nation Victoria candidate, South-East Metro, Legislative Council candidate

Australian parents are being sold a lie about what is happening in our education system.

Instead of concentrating on knowledge, literacy, numeracy, science, history and civics, schools are being used to shape children's beliefs about race, climate, identity, sexuality, inequality and social justice.

Tue, 25 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/education-not-indoctrination Senator Pauline Hanson and Barnaby Joyce Call for Section 18C to Be Scrapped
At the heart of the battle for free speech is section 18C of the Racial Discrimination Act. Barnaby was right, it needs to be scrapped. The impact that section 18C has had on free speech in this country and democracy has been chilling. Pauline’s recent court battles have made this very clear. Robust political debate is critical for our democracy.
Tue, 25 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/scrap-section-18c Colleen Harkin: Keep Political Activism Out of Victorian Classrooms

Parliament has passed it. Every school, Prep to Year 12, now has to teach Australian history through the “activism” lens pushed by the Yoorrook Commission.

Mon, 24 Aug 2026 +1000 One Nation http://www.onenation.org.au/victoria-history-curriculum

snapshots.captured_representation: Hansard - Parliament of Victoria Skip to content Parliamentary activity Hansard Hansard is the official report of the proceedings of the Parliament of Victoria from 1866 to the present day. It is a comprehensive record of the debates that shape legislation and the speeches that inform policymaking in Victoria. Proceedings from 1856 to 1866 were reported in the Argus newspaper. Hansard captures key issues affecting Victorians, the government’s priorities, the views and policies of opposition parties and concerns individuals or groups have raised with their local member. Hansard is published progressively on sitting days. You can find a member’s speech on Browse Hansard within 3 hours. A proof version of the full day’s proceedings is published 4 hours after the sitting day has finished. A final version of Hansard is available five working days later. Browse Hansard and Argus records by day or week (1851–present) Search Hansard by keyword (1991–present) Editorial policy Hansard’s publishing team corrects for grammar and obvious factual errors. Hansard is substantially verbatim and some parliamentary formalities are shown in summarised form – for example, divisions (votes) and procedural motions. Members can review Hansard and suggest corrections to obvious errors, such as incorrect dates, names or figures, but they cannot ask for changes that alter the meaning of their speech. Interjections The Speaker of the Legislative Assembly and President of the Legislative Council give members the call – their turn to speak. Interjections are not usually recorded in Hansard unless they are responded to and relate directly to the matter at hand. Incorporated material and quotes Some parts of the Hansard report are incorporated, which means the words were not spoken in the chamber. This material is clearly indicated in Hansard. Similarly, when members quote at length from articles, letters or emails, this material will be indented. Hansard requires members to provide the sources of their quotes. Committees While the Hansard publishing team produces parliamentary committee transcripts, committees are responsible for publishing the transcripts. These can be found on the committees pages on the Parliament of Victoria website. More about committees Argus reports From 1851 to 1856, Victoria had only one legislative body, the Legislative Council, which held its proceedings at St Patrick’s Hall in Bourke Street, Melbourne. Proceedings of the Council were reported in the Argus newspaper. Argus editorials concerning the Legislative Council have been included with reports of the proceedings. The Argus reports can be found in Browse Hansard . There are different ways to search Hansard depending on what you are looking for. If you know the specific date, view Hansard by day on the Hansard search page. Update : The Hansard Search will now return refined results for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). This is part of an ongoing project to migrate past Hansards into a modern advanced search platform. Please report any issues to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au . How to search Hansard Frequently asked questions How to find committee transcripts When is Hansard available? Support How to search Hansard 2021 - current (41st and 42nd Parliaments) Hansard search Note: The 41st Parliament (2021-2024) is now included in these search results. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a member from the dropdown list Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Multiple proceedings may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a proceeding from the dropdown list Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. Results can be further refined by selecting the metadata in the left-hand side of the screen. Electorate House Members Ministry Proceeding Subproceeding Parliament. Clicking ‘Download PDF’ in the top right-hand corner will download a print-ready version of the proceeding. Clicking 'Daily PDF' will download the full day Hansard currently available. Note, this document is generated from the online version which can be subject to further correction. See Hansard Publication below. Boolean operators The Hansard search requires all words in your query to appear in the result. So, if you search for maternity hospital , you'll only get results that contain both words. The Boolean operators AND, OR, and NOT only work as operators when your search terms are wrapped in double quotes. Without quotes, they're treated as ordinary search words. What you want How to search Example Either term (OR) "term1" OR "term2" "maternity" OR "hospital" Exclude a term (NOT) "term1" NOT "term2" "maternity" NOT "hospital" Both terms required (AND) "term1" AND "term2" "maternity" AND "hospital" Either term (alternative) term1 | term2 maternity | hospital Exact phrase "multi word phrase" "maternity hospital" What's NOT supported Proximity/numerical connectors for finding terms within a certain word distance are not available in the current search. Parliamentary debates August 2000 to November 2024 (35th to 41st Parliaments) Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament (35th to 41st Parliaments only) House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly. You can also search for Assembly legislation committees or Assembly estimates. Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected. Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Committees: Search for references to standing committees in Parliament. Dates: Select a custom date search by Year Date Date range. Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Page no.: Search for a particular page in the final Hansard. Results per page: the default is 100 Sort order: Select the order in which you want your results displayed Search results Click on the date on the left side to bring up the PDF of that proceeding. Click on the PDF symbol on the right to access the Hansard of the entire day. Results can be further refined by adding more filters to the advanced search on the results page. Update: Hansard Search filters now apply to speeches for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). The Refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) will remain available during this transition. Historical Hansard 1870 to July 2000 Hansard search Hansards between 1870 to 2000 have been scanned from the printed bound volumes and search results may not always be reliable. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Note : Filters for bills, proceedings and members will not work for Hansards prior to 2021. Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. The Hansard indexes provide information about member speeches and subjects, and can be used to assist your search. Find the indexes here: Hansard Indexes . For those who were familiar with the previous method of searching the 1870-2000 Hansards, the search is available here Frequently asked questions How can I find all the speeches made by a particular member? You can find all of a current member’s speeches in their member’s page on the Parliament website, by navigating to Current Members and searching or browsing for the member. Member speeches are separated into two categories: Speeches prior to 2021, returning refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) results Speeches from 2021 onwards, returning results using the current Hansard Search . To search for speeches by former members, use the Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) , select the Member filter, and press Search. For members who served prior to 2000, use the Historical Search or the Hansard Search to free text search their name and/or topic. How can I read what was said on a bill? The Bills section of the public website displays a history on each bill page, a copy of the bill, the explanatory memorandum and a link to second reading speeches. To find further debates in the Hansard search, select the relevant bill from the dropdown list and select Search. How can I find the broadcast for a particular speech? Videos of parliamentary debates from April 2021 are available on our Video Archives . Why are there multiple Hansard searches? We are progressively upgrading the Hansard search to provide a more modern, consistent and powerful way to search parliamentary records. Hansard is the official record of parliamentary debates and a historically significant resource, and it is important that users can easily and reliably find information within Hansard. Because historical Hansard records have been created and stored in different formats over many years, upgrading the search is a complex process. Each Parliament must be carefully reviewed and prepared before it can be added to the new system. During this project, multiple search tools will remain available. How to find committee transcripts Committee transcripts are published in the committees section of the public website, for both current and past committees. When is Hansard available? Hansard is published progressively throughout the sitting day, with the full version generally appearing online within three hours of the house rising. This is a draft version, with the final, corrected Hansard appearing two to three days after the sitting. Finalised Hansard is available: for Tuesday by <TIME> Friday for Wednesday by <TIME> Monday following a sitting week for Thursday by <TIME> Tuesday following a sitting week. Please note: Public holidays may result in delays. Although we encourage the use of the Hansard record, the draft should not be quoted as it may be subject to further correction. Any changes made to the draft Hansard will be automatically reflected online. Support For assistance with Hansard or Broadcast, please reach out to the Reporting Services team on hansard@parliament.wa.gov.au For assistance with accessing and using parliamentary systems or using the public website, please reach out to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au or 08 9222 7200 . continuing to benefit from more timely access to urgent care, with the Long Jetty Urgent Care Service providing more than 32,700 patient attendances since opening in December 2023. Ministerial media release 8 September 2026 Minns Labor Government delivering more local training opportunities to help strengthen regional workforces People living in regional and remote NSW will have greater access to training, support and employment opportunities closer to home, as the Minns Labor Government continues to rebuild TAFE NSW and restore pathways into skilled careers across regional communities. Ministerial media release 8 September 2026 First look: Woollahra long-term housing transformation Thousands more people could have the opportunity to call Woollahra and Edgecliff home under the Minns Labor Government’s new vision to deliver up to 9,400 new homes around Sydney’s first new heavy rail station in more than a decade. Ministerial media release 8 September 2026 NSW households to benefit from community-led energy support Households across NSW will get more help to cut their energy bills, access rebates and make energy-saving upgrades, with the Minns Labor Government investing $4.7 million in 12 community and not-for-profit energy organisations. Ministerial media release 8 September 2026 Big boost in homes for Parramatta Metro station development Parramatta’s city centre will get a housing and student accommodation boost just footsteps from the world class Metro West, with 470 homes and 500 student units set to be delivered by the consortium contracted to build the Metro station and integrated development. Ministerial media release 8 September 2026 NSW Health Secretary Susan Pearce After more than 30 years of outstanding service to NSW Health, including almost five years as Secretary, Ms Susan Pearce AM has advised me of her intention to retire at the end of March 2027. Ministerial media release 7 September 2026 Largest CBD Solar Farm in Southern Hemisphere coming to ICC Sydney The Minns Labor Government is leading the way on urban renewables and sustainability with the government owned International Convention Centre (ICC) Sydney set to become home to the largest solar farm in any Central Business District in the Southern Hemisphere. Ministerial media release 7 September 2026 NSW Government backs councils to host major multicultural festivals The Minns Labor Government is providing $2.5 million in grant funding to help local councils across NSW deliver major multicultural festivals that will light up the calendar next year. Ministerial media release 7 September 2026 Design released for long-awaited Spring Farm Parkway extension The Minns and Albanese Labor Governments are today unveiling the proposed design for Spring Farm Parkway Stage 2, a three-kilometre, four-lane road that would complete the east-west link between Menangle Park and Spring Farm. Ministerial media release 7 September 2026 Minns Government delivers $350,000 boost for Rehab In The Home in southern Lake Macquarie The Minns Government is investing $350,000 to expand Rehab In The Home services across southern Lake Macquarie, helping more people access rehabilitation and recovery services closer to home. keyboard_arrow_left 1 2 3 ... 640 keyboard_arrow_right You may also be interested in Have your say Contact a Minister NSW Government Facebook Top of page north This page is managed by Department of Customer Service Your rating will help us improve the website. snapshots.captured_representation: Parliament of WA Web - hansard how to search and use hansard Skip to main content Home Site map Accessibility Contact us Alerts Home Menu Show/Hide website navigation The Legislative Assembly meets today (<TIME>) Watch live Watch Assembly live The Legislative Council meets today (<TIME>) Watch live Watch Council live The Community Development meets today (<TIME>) Watch live Watch Committee live Search this website Advanced Search Search Parliamentary Business Bills (proposed laws) WA Acts and Regulations (current Laws) Hansard (Debates) Committees Tabled Papers Chamber Documents Parliamentary Questions and Answers Sitting Calendar Order of Business Standing Orders Watch and listen Scrutiny of finances (Budget Estimates) Members Find your MP Members of the Legislative Council (Upper House) President and Office Holders Upper House Seating Plan Members of the Legislative Assembly (Lower House) Speaker and Office Holders Lower House Seating Plan What Members do Ministers and Parliamentary Secretaries Shadow Ministers Members’ biographical register Electorates About Parliament Legislative Council (Upper House) Legislative Assembly (Lower House) Parliamentary Departments Parliament Plans & Publications Careers Get Involved Find Your MP Find out what was said in Parliament Watch and listen Make a submission Petitioning Parliament Public hearings Contact a member Vote in an election Lighting of Parliament Parliamentary Friendship Groups Former Members Association What Parliament does RSS Feeds / Alerts Visit and Learn Tours Education Programs and Resources Plan your visit Events and exhibitions Parliamentary History Parliamentary Library House and Grounds How Parliament works Fact sheets Parliaments and Sessions How to search and use Hansard Home How to search and use Hansard The Hansard search includes the records of debates of the Legislative Council and Legislative Assembly from 1870 to the present day. There are different ways to search Hansard depending on what you are looking for. If you know the specific date, view Hansard by day on the Hansard search page. Update : The Hansard Search will now return refined results for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). This is part of an ongoing project to migrate past Hansards into a modern advanced search platform. Please report any issues to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au . How to search Hansard Frequently asked questions How to find committee transcripts When is Hansard available? Support How to search Hansard 2021 - current (41st and 42nd Parliaments) Hansard search Note: The 41st Parliament (2021-2024) is now included in these search results. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a member from the dropdown list Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Multiple proceedings may be selected by pressing SHIFT when selecting a proceeding from the dropdown list Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. Results can be further refined by selecting the metadata in the left-hand side of the screen. Electorate House Members Ministry Proceeding Subproceeding Parliament. Clicking ‘Download PDF’ in the top right-hand corner will download a print-ready version of the proceeding. Clicking 'Daily PDF' will download the full day Hansard currently available. Note, this document is generated from the online version which can be subject to further correction. See Hansard Publication below. Boolean operators The Hansard search requires all words in your query to appear in the result. So, if you search for maternity hospital , you'll only get results that contain both words. The Boolean operators AND, OR, and NOT only work as operators when your search terms are wrapped in double quotes. Without quotes, they're treated as ordinary search words. What you want How to search Example Either term (OR) "term1" OR "term2" "maternity" OR "hospital" Exclude a term (NOT) "term1" NOT "term2" "maternity" NOT "hospital" Both terms required (AND) "term1" AND "term2" "maternity" AND "hospital" Either term (alternative) term1 | term2 maternity | hospital Exact phrase "multi word phrase" "maternity hospital" What's NOT supported Proximity/numerical connectors for finding terms within a certain word distance are not available in the current search. Parliamentary debates August 2000 to November 2024 (35th to 41st Parliaments) Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament (35th to 41st Parliaments only) House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly. You can also search for Assembly legislation committees or Assembly estimates. Member: Search by the member who spoke on a particular topic. Multiple members may be selected. Bill: Find all search results on a particular bill Committees: Search for references to standing committees in Parliament. Dates: Select a custom date search by Year Date Date range. Proceeding: Find all search results on a parliamentary proceeding, e.g. second reading, grievance, petition. Page no.: Search for a particular page in the final Hansard. Results per page: the default is 100 Sort order: Select the order in which you want your results displayed Search results Click on the date on the left side to bring up the PDF of that proceeding. Click on the PDF symbol on the right to access the Hansard of the entire day. Results can be further refined by adding more filters to the advanced search on the results page. Update: Hansard Search filters now apply to speeches for the 41st and 42nd Parliament (2021-current day). The Refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) will remain available during this transition. Historical Hansard 1870 to July 2000 Hansard search Hansards between 1870 to 2000 have been scanned from the printed bound volumes and search results may not always be reliable. Use keyword search for general words or phrases. Use quotation marks to search for an exact phrase. Use filters to refine your search. Parliament: select the four-year term of Parliament House: Legislative Council or Legislative Assembly Date range Note : Filters for bills, proceedings and members will not work for Hansards prior to 2021. Select ‘Apply filter’ to run your search. Search results The default display order for search results is newest to oldest. The Hansard indexes provide information about member speeches and subjects, and can be used to assist your search. Find the indexes here: Hansard Indexes . For those who were familiar with the previous method of searching the 1870-2000 Hansards, the search is available here Frequently asked questions How can I find all the speeches made by a particular member? You can find all of a current member’s speeches in their member’s page on the Parliament website, by navigating to Current Members and searching or browsing for the member. Member speeches are separated into two categories: Speeches prior to 2021, returning refined Hansard search (2000 - 2024) results Speeches from 2021 onwards, returning results using the current Hansard Search . To search for speeches by former members, use the Refined Hansard search (2000-2024) , select the Member filter, and press Search. For members who served prior to 2000, use the Historical Search or the Hansard Search to free text search their name and/or topic. How can I read what was said on a bill? The Bills section of the public website displays a history on each bill page, a copy of the bill, the explanatory memorandum and a link to second reading speeches. To find further debates in the Hansard search, select the relevant bill from the dropdown list and select Search. How can I find the broadcast for a particular speech? Videos of parliamentary debates from April 2021 are available on our Video Archives . Why are there multiple Hansard searches? We are progressively upgrading the Hansard search to provide a more modern, consistent and powerful way to search parliamentary records. Hansard is the official record of parliamentary debates and a historically significant resource, and it is important that users can easily and reliably find information within Hansard. Because historical Hansard records have been created and stored in different formats over many years, upgrading the search is a complex process. Each Parliament must be carefully reviewed and prepared before it can be added to the new system. During this project, multiple search tools will remain available. How to find committee transcripts Committee transcripts are published in the committees section of the public website, for both current and past committees. When is Hansard available? Hansard is published progressively throughout the sitting day, with the full version generally appearing online within three hours of the house rising. This is a draft version, with the final, corrected Hansard appearing two to three days after the sitting. Finalised Hansard is available: for Tuesday by <TIME> Friday for Wednesday by <TIME> Monday following a sitting week for Thursday by <TIME> Tuesday following a sitting week. Please note: Public holidays may result in delays. Although we encourage the use of the Hansard record, the draft should not be quoted as it may be subject to further correction. Any changes made to the draft Hansard will be automatically reflected online. Support For assistance with Hansard or Broadcast, please reach out to the Reporting Services team on hansard@parliament.wa.gov.au For assistance with accessing and using parliamentary systems or using the public website, please reach out to itservicedesk@parliament.wa.gov.au or 08 9222 7200 . Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said Cardew received 48.28 per cent of the first preference votes in the by-election, winning the position of Mayor ahead of candidate Mark Norvall. The election was conducted by full postal ballot. “Election day was 22 August, and voters have 10 days to return their postal votes to be included in the count,” Mr Vidgen said. “The outcome is now certain as the number of votes outstanding cannot change the result. Voters still need to return their postal vote to be counted before 5pm on Tuesday 1 September.” Mr Vidgen said that of the 21,058 people enrolled in Tablelands Regional Council, 14,771 ballot papers have been returned and counted so far resulting in a turnout of 70.14%. Nominations were open from Tuesday 21 July 2026 with 5 candidates nominating to represent their community. Tablelands Regional Council by-election information and results are available at the ECQ website . The ballot order draw was conducted in Deeragun following the close of nominations at noon today. Candidates in ballot paper order are: Michelle HOBSON Steven CLARE Michael PUGH Shayne BLACKLOCK Joanne KEUNE Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said he was pleased to see candidates willing to represent the community ahead of the Saturday 19 September by-election. “With the order of the ballot paper finalised, we will begin printing and mailing your ballot packs,” Mr Vidgen said. “All people enrolled in Townsville City Council Division 1 will receive their pack in the post. There will be no polling places to vote in person.” When you receive your postal ballot pack, it is very important to follow the instructions on your ballot paper to ensure your vote counts. This includes signing the declaration envelope and making sure the envelope is also signed by a witness. “For your vote to count, we must receive your completed ballot paper by 5pm Tuesday 29 September 2026,” he said. Mr Vidgen reminded the 17,000 enrolled voters in Townsville Division 1 that voting is compulsory and failure to vote may attract a $172 fine. Keep up to date with the Townsville City Council Division 1 by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us at 1300 881 665 for more information. The Electoral Commission of Queensland (ECQ) confirmed the by-election will be a full postal ballot for all enrolled Division 1 residents. There will be no polling places to vote in person. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said ballot packs will be sent to every enrolled voter in Division 1. “We know that residents in this division have been required to vote in several recent by-elections, so our focus is on making the voting process as easy as possible.” “We will send a ballot pack to the postal address of each voter, so it’s important to make sure your enrolment details are up to date,” Mr Vidgen said. If you added a postal address to the electoral roll, your pack will be mailed to that address instead of to your residential address. If you need your ballot pack mailed to a different address, have moved and need to change your address or are enrolling for the first time, you must update your details or enrol by 5pm on 17 August 2026 at the Australian Electoral Commission’s website . “Nominations for the vacant Councillor position are now open,” Mr Vidgen said. Anyone interested in representing their community must nominate before 12 noon on Thursday 20 August 2026. “To nominate as a candidate, you first need to ensure you’re eligible,” Mr Vidgen said. “The best place to start is the local government election participants page of the ECQ’s website.” Potential candidates must: pay a deposit of $250 open a dedicated campaign bank account complete the free ‘So you want to be a councillor’ online training through the Department of Local Government, Water and Volunteers (unless they are a sitting councillor) be endorsed by at least 6 eligible voters currently enrolled in Division 1 of Townsville City Council. “Postal voting packs will be sent shortly after the close of nominations and the draw for ballot paper order is finalised,” said Mr Vidgen. “Please keep an eye out for your pack in the mail.” Keep up to date with the Townsville City Council Division 1 by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. The election was conducted by full postal ballot. “Election day was 20 June, and voters had 10 days to return their postal votes to be included in the count,” Mr Vidgen said. “That deadline passed yesterday at 5pm on Tuesday 30 June.” Mr Vidgen said that of the 867 people enrolled in Winton Shire Council, 728 ballot papers were completed and returned on time resulting in a turnout of 84%. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said the result of the by-election will not be declared until after the cut-off for the return of completed postal ballots on Tuesday 30 June 2026. “Counting got underway at 6pm on Saturday 20 June in the presence of scrutineers and will continue as more postal votes are received,” Mr Vidgen explained. “As of last night, a total of 636 votes have been counted which is about 73.4% of voters in the Winton Shire.” “The declaration of a successful candidate can only be made when the outcome is certain. “While voters needed to complete their ballot papers by 6pm on Saturday, we are still receiving votes through the mail for this full postal by-election,” he said. Voters who completed their vote last Saturday but forgot to drop it in the post box can still mail their vote to us, or if it’s more convenient, they can drop it off in-person at the post office in Winton. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen announced the result today. “Stafford voters have spoken, and Luke Richmond will now represent the electorate in the Queensland Parliament.” More than 13,530 people voted early, around 5,000 voted by post and a further 370 by telephone. 14,300 people voted on election day. “Election day was last Saturday, 16 May. The small number of postal votes outstanding cannot change the result, so the outcome is now certain,” Mr Vidgen said. “Counting will continue, and postal voters will still need to return their vote before 6pm on Tuesday, 26 May for it to be included in the count.” Mr Vidgen said that around 41,000 residents were enrolled in the Stafford electorate, and around 33,700 votes have been counted, resulting in a turnout of 81.45%. Nominations were open from 18 April 2026 with 9 candidates nominating. Keep up to date with the Stafford by-election results on the ECQ website. 21 May 2026 - Stafford by-election count continues Vote counting in the Stafford State by-election is continuing. So far, Electoral Commission of Queensland staff have counted around: 13,530 early votes 14,300 election day votes 4,800 postal votes 370 telephone votes 160 declaration votes. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen says the official count for the Stafford by-election is underway but that a declaration won’t be made until the outcome is mathematically beyond doubt. “Voters have until 6pm on Tuesday 26 May 2026 to return any outstanding postal votes to us,” he explained. “While we are closely monitoring the progress of the count since the contest is close, we may need to wait until all votes have been received and counted.” Once the results are finalised, the ECQ will consider its approach to non-voters, with 80% of the electorate turning out to vote. “Even at a by-election, voting is compulsory, and penalties apply for failing to vote” Mr Vidgen said. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said staff in both areas were counting the first preferences from the votes taken on election day, during early voting, telephone voting and the postal votes returned so far. “Voting finished at 6pm for both by-elections, but it could still take a few days to determine the results,” he said. “We’ll only declare successful candidates when the outcome is certain.” Stafford State by-election Across the inner north Brisbane electorate, there were more than: 13,530 early voters 370 telephone voters 14,260 people who voted on election day 3,860 postal votes returned. You can check if you live in the Stafford electorate by using the ECQ’s Where is my electorate? tool. Keep up to date with the Stafford by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us at 1300 881 665 for more information. 5 May 2026 - Early voting starts today for Stafford by-election Voting is underway in the Stafford State by-election, with early voting kicking off at 8am this morning. Two early voting centres will be taking votes in the lead up to election day on Saturday 16 May and will be open between 8am and 6pm on weekdays through to Friday, 15 May. Early voting centres: Chermside Kedron Community Church, Cnr Rode & Gympie Roads, Kedron Wilston Grange Australian Football Club, Hickey Park, Babarra Street, Stafford Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen encouraged people to take advantage of early voting. “We’re committed to making voting as convenient and easy as possible for voters. You can bring the maroon Voter Information Card, or the email version of this, to the booth with you to help our officials mark you off the roll quickly,” he said. “While there’s just one ballot paper to fill out for this by-election, it’s important to number every box in the order of your preference for your vote to count. On election day, Saturday 16 May 2026, there will be 12 polling booths around the Stafford electorate. Details about the by-election, including eligibility for telephone voting, can be found on the ECQ website at ecq.qld.gov.au/Stafford . The Stafford electorate includes the Brisbane suburbs of Chermside, Newmarket, Stafford Heights, Kedron and more. You can check if you live in the Stafford electorate by using the ECQ’s Where is my electorate? tool. Keep up to date with the Stafford by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us at 1300 881 665 for more information. April 24 April 2026 - Stafford by-election candidates announced Nine candidates will contest the seat of Stafford at the upcoming State by-election. The ballot draw was conducted in Kedron today, following the close of nominations at noon. Candidates will be listed on the ballot paper in the following order: Luke Richmond (Australian Labor Party) Jacqueline Verne (Legalise Cannabis Qld (Party)) Damian Smart (Independent) Daniel Selff (Libertarians) Liam Parry (Independent) Jess Lane (The Greens) Lucy O'Brien (Animal Justice Party) Alan Denaro (Family First) Fiona Hammond (LNP) Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said 9 was a strong field of candidates for a by-election. “Now that voters know who is running, they can decide who they want to represent them,” Mr Vidgen said. “With the candidates confirmed, the ballot papers will now be printed and ready for the start of early voting on 5 May.” More than 41,000 voters enrolled in the electorate can plan how they’ll have their say, by choosing from the below voting options. To vote early, go to the Chermside Kedron Community Church in Kedron or Wilston Grange Australian Football Club in Stafford from Tuesday 5 May until Friday 15 May. Early voting will be available on weekdays from 8am to 6pm. To vote on election day, Saturday 16 May 2026, visit one of 12 polling booths around the Stafford electorate. Mr Vidgen said there are also options for those who can’t vote in person at a polling booth. “If people can’t cast their ballots in person, they can request a postal vote, and telephone voting will also be available to those who meet certain criteria,” he said. Postal vote requests are open until 7pm on 4 May 2026. Details about the by-election, including eligibility for telephone voting, can be found on the ECQ website. The Stafford electorate includes the Brisbane suburbs of Chermside, Newmarket, Stafford Heights, Kedron and more. You can check if you live in the Stafford electorate by using the ECQ’s Where is my electorate? tool. Keep up to date with the Stafford by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us at 1300 881 665 for more information. 23 April 2026 - Central Highlands Regional Council by-election candidates announced Five candidates will contest the vacant Councillor position at the upcoming Central Highlands Regional Council by-election. The ballot paper draw was conducted in Emerald today, following the close of nominations at noon. Candidates will be listed on the ballot paper in the following order: Amanda Phillott Bronwyn Dalton Edward Shaw Christine Wilson Sharyn Leigh Heiskari Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said he was pleased to see the field of candidates willing to put their hand up to represent their community. “Now that voters know who is running for the vacant position, they can decide who they want to represent them on their local Council,” he said. “With the candidates determined, the ballot papers will now be printed and ready for the start of early voting on Tuesday, 5 May 2026.” Now’s a great time to plan how you will have your say, by choosing from the below voting options. To vote early, go to Wally McKenzie House, Emerald Show Grounds between 9am and 6pm weekdays from Tuesday, 5 May to Friday, 15 May 2026. To vote on election day, visit one of 10 polling locations between 8am and 6pm on Saturday, 16 May 2026. If you’ll be away on election day, you can request a postal vote. Applications for postal votes will close at 7pm on Monday, 4 May 2026. This by-election was triggered by the resignation of Councillor Gai Sypher on 23 March 2026. Keep up to date with the Central Highlands Regional Council by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us on 1300 881 665 for more information. 17 April 2026 - Stafford State by-election called for Saturday 16 May 2026 A State by-election in the electorate of Stafford is underway following the issue of the writ by the Governor of Queensland today. Around 41,000 voters in Stafford will vote to choose a new Member of Parliament, with election day set for Saturday 16 May 2026. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said nominations will open at 9am tomorrow for anyone interested in representing their community. Nominations will close at 12 noon on Friday 24 April 2026. “To nominate as a candidate, you need to take a number of important steps, including ensuring you’re eligible to nominate,” Mr Vidgen said. “If you’re interested in nominating, I strongly encourage you to start preparing now. The best place to start is by looking at the information for potential candidates which is available on the State government election participants page of the ECQ’s website.” Mr Vidgen said voters in Stafford will have access to a range of voting options. “We know that convenience is important for voters, and we’ll be making a range of voting options available for this by-election. This includes early voting and postal voting. “Early voting will be open from 8am to 6pm on weekdays between Tuesday 5 May and Friday 15 May. “If you’re planning to vote on election day, there will be a number of polling booths open across the electorate. However, we know that it’s not always possible for people to get to a polling booth in person and that some people may be away during the by-election. “If you want to vote by post, you can request a postal ballot online now. Some voters may also be eligible to vote by telephone. More information on these options is available at ecq.qld.gov.au/Stafford.” The Stafford electorate includes the Brisbane suburbs of Chermside, Newmarket, Stafford, Stafford Heights, Kedron and more. You can check if you live in the Stafford electorate by using the ECQ’s Where is my electorate? tool. Keep up to date with the Stafford State by-election at the ECQ’s website ecq.qld.gov.au/Stafford or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us at 1300 881 665 for more information. 14 April 2026 - Central Highlands Regional Council by-election announced for 16 May 2026 A by-election for the vacant Councillor position on the Central Highlands Regional Council will be held on Saturday 16 May 2026. Electoral Commissioner Pat Vidgen said nominations for the councillor position are now open for anyone interested in representing their community. Those interested are encouraged to start preparing now, with nominations closing at 12 noon on Thursday, 23 April 2026. “To nominate as a candidate, you need to take a number of important steps, including ensuring you’re eligible to nominate and enrolled in the Central Highlands Regional Council area,” Mr Vidgen said. Other requirements are: paying a deposit of $250 opening a dedicated bank account completing the mandatory candidate training course ‘So you want to be a councillor’ online at the Department of Local Government, Water and Volunteers website. Prospective candidates are also urged to visit the Election Participants page of the ECQ’s website for more information about nominating. Mr Vidgen said Central Highlands residents should also be preparing to vote by checking they are correctly enrolled. “You can ensure you have a say about your next councillor by taking a few moments to check your enrolment details. If you have changed your address or are enrolling to vote for the first time, you’ll need to do this by Monday 20 April 2026,” he said. To enrol to vote, check your enrolment or update your details, visit the Australian Electoral Commission’s website . This by-election was triggered by the resignation of Councillor Gai Sypher on 23 March 2026. Keep up to date with the Central Highlands Regional Council by-election at the ECQ’s website or on social media @electoralcommissionqld. You can also call us on 1300 881 665 for more information. March 31 March 2026 - Objections against State electoral redistribution closing soon The third stage of public consultation relating to the current State electoral redistribution is closing soon. The Queensland Redistribution Commission (QRC) has published its proposed electoral redistribution on the State’s electoral districts, and invited objections against the proposed redistribution before Thursday 9 April 2026. The QRC has released a report on the proposed redistribution, which includes: maps showing the boundaries of the 93 proposed electoral districts the names and boundary descriptions of all proposed electoral districts the Commission’s reasons for redistributing the State in the way proposed The report is available for public inspection without fee on the QRC’s website at redistribution.ecq.qld.gov.au , at the Electoral Commission of Queensland offices at Level 20, 1 Eagle Street, Brisbane and at the electorate offices of State Members of Parliament. Any person or body may object against the proposed electoral redistribution during the 30-day period closing on 9 April 2026. Objections can be lodged in writing until Thursday, 9 April 2026 via: Online form: ecq.qld.gov.au/QRCconsultation Email: QRCsubmissions@ecq.qld.gov.au Mail: Queensland Redistribution Commission GPO Box 1393, Brisbane QLD 4001 Following the close of this stage of public consultation, the QRC will publish all objections on the QRC website. The public will then be invited to comment on the objections between 20-30 April 2026 in the final stage of public consultation. In accordance with section 50 of the Electoral Act 1992, the QRC will then consider the objections and comments and make any necessary changes to the proposed electoral redistribution. 16 March 2026 - Pormpuraaw Aboriginal Shire Council by-election declared The Electoral Commission of Queensland (ECQ) has declared Devon Tarpencha the successful candidate for the Pormpuraaw Aboriginal Shire Council by-election. The by-election was triggered by the resignation of Councillor Lucy Foote on 31 January 2026. Pormpuraaw Aboriginal Shire Council by-election information, including all results, is available at on the ECQ website or visit ecq.qld.gov.au/pormpuraaw and select ‘view the by-election result’. Early voting: between 9am and 6pm from Wednesday 11 March to Friday 13 March 2026. Close of Electoral Roll Only Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people on the South Australian electoral roll can vote in the South Australian First Nations Voice Election. Ensure you are enrolled, and your details are up to date by 5pm, Friday, 27 February 2026. If you are unsure whether you are on the electoral roll, you can check your enrolment online at savoiceelection.sa.gov.au. Have you recently turned 18 or changed your residential address? Any Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander person can nominate to stand as a candidate in the South Australian First Nations Voice Election as long as they meet the relevant eligibility criteria. More information on eligibility criteria is available at savoiceelection.sa.gov.au. Local First Nations Voice vacancies are set out below: Region 1 — Kumangka Warrarna Wangkanthi (Central) —11 vacancies. 5 Male/5 Female/1 Any Gender. Unsuccessful candidates from a previous supplementary election are contacted, and a recount of the votes is conducted including those candidates who have confirmed that they are still willing and have been found to still be eligible to nominate for the position. Alice Cashen A/RETURNING OFFICER More information https://ecsa.sa.gov.au/2025-adelaide-central MEDIA | CITY OF ADELAIDE Central ward Supplementary Election to occur Details Published: 11 April 2025 Adelaide, South Australia 11 April 2025 The Electoral Commission of South Australia (ECSA) is committed to maintaining confidence in the electoral process and ensuring integrity in voter enrolments. Following today’s court decision, an election for the City of Adelaide Council Central Ward will be conducted as soon as practicable. The supplementary election process will take approximately three months from the close of roll, which is set for 30 May 2025, in accordance with legislative requirements. This timing enables the Council to update its voters roll in accordance with relevant legislative requirements. ECSA treats any instance of interference in the electoral process seriously and will continue to strengthen safeguards. ECSA will continue to take action to maintain the integrity of the electoral process through rigorous checks and monitoring, and work with Councils to review the enrolment forms that are submitted to them for unusual enrolment activity. Alice Cashen, A/Electoral Commissioner for South Australia (ECSA) says, "ECSA remains steadfast in its commitment to fair and transparent elections. Every measure we take, whether through scrutiny processes, investigative efforts, or proposed legislative improvements is aimed at ensuring public confidence in our electoral system. ECSA treats any instance of interference in the electoral process seriously." To further strengthen electoral integrity, ECSA’s 2022 Council Election Report recommends that electors be required to provide identification and proof of residence when enrolling and further powers to reject returned voting papers where the date of birth provided does not correspond with the date of birth of the elector. These measures aim to prevent fraudulent activity and uphold the transparency of the electoral process. ECSA’s A/Commissioner reaffirmed, “ ECSA had taken immediate action to investigate concerns raised during the 2022 Council election process. ECSA had detected instances of voter fraud and acted decisively to protect the integrity of the election, by holding out suspect ballot paper envelopes, verifying enrolments, and contacting electors directly, to ensure that only legitimate votes were counted .” Media enquiries All requests will be responded to in a timely manner. DOWNLOAD PDF Today the Minister for Local Government, the Hon Joe Szakacs MP tabled in Parliament the Electoral Commission of South Australia report into the 2022 Council Elections. The 2022 local government periodic elections (2022 Council Elections) were conducted for 66 of the 67 councils within South Australia to elect representatives to a total of 683 positions. The elections commenced with the close of rolls on Friday 29 July 2022 and concluded with the final formal declaration of results on Monday 28 November 2022. At the close of rolls, the total number of enrolled electors was 1,288,329 compared to 1,213,862 for the 2018 Council Elections. Nominations closed at 12 noon, Tuesday 6 September 2022 with 1,256 nominations accepted compared to 1,374 in 2018. What is the South Australian First Nations Voice to Parliament Election, what are supplementary elections, and who can vote? The South Australian First Nations Voice to Parliament Election is the process for the Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders of South Australia to elect their representatives to the South Australian First Nations Voice to Parliament. Through the Voice, First Nations people have their say at the highest levels of decision-making in South Australia, including to Parliament, on matters, policies and laws that affect them. The Voice is an advisory body and does not have veto powers or decision-making powers in South Australia’s Parliament. It allows the opportunity for Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people to raise community priorities in a public, transparent, and accountable way. Only Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islanders enrolled in South Australia can vote and nominate as a candidate in the election. Voting in the SA First Nations Voice to Parliament Election is not compulsory. There are 6 regions across South Australia, with an elected body for each. All elected members are Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people and are elected by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people who live in their region. Of the 6 regions: Five have 7 elected members One (the Central Local First Nations Voice region) has 11 elected members, as it has a higher population of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander people. Due to the resignation of SA Voice members, supplementary elections are needed to fill vacant positions in Regions 1 Kumangka Warrarna Wangkanthi (Central) and Region 4 Murraylands, Riverland and South East (Riverland & South East). MEDIA STATEMENT: Adelaide Plains - Result of second petition Details Published: 23 December 2024 Media statement from the Electoral Commission of SA (ECSA) Adelaide Plains - Result of second petition FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: 23/12/2024 Adelaide, South Australia The Court of Disputed Returns has made orders finalising the second petition filed by the Electoral Commissioner seeking to correct the outcome of the 2022 election in the Adelaide Plains Council area. The Commissioner filed two petitions after identifying an error in the settings of the computer software used to count votes in complex elections, which he considered affected the outcome of the election in the Adelaide Plains Council area and a recount conducted following the resignation of a former Adelaide Plains Councillor. In its judgment, the Court stressed that the error in the counting and declaration of votes was solely the responsibility of the Commissioner, and there was no reason to think the former councillors brought about their removal from office or did not fulfil their functions as councillors with enthusiasm and diligence. As a result of the second petition, the Court has now declared Mr Carmine Di Troia not duly elected. The Court has ordered that a recount be conducted to fill the casual vacancy. Work is underway to prepare for the recount which will be conducted in early January 2025. The Commissioner welcomes the finalisation of both petitions and apologises for the impact of the error on each of the respondents and the Adelaide Plains Council.
